title: Optimality Of Universal Conclusive Entanglement Concentration Protocols
authors: Alexandre C. Orthey, Jr., Aby Philip, Tulja Varun Kondra, And Alexander Streltsov
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre C. Orthey, Jr., Aby Philip, Tulja Varun Kondra, and Alexander Streltsov

Entanglement concentration is essential for quantum technologies yet, rigorous bounds on the success probability for universal protocols (those requiring no prior knowledge about the input state) have remained underexplored. We establish such fundamental limits for conclusive protocols distilling a …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062404] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on the success probability of universal conclusive entanglement concentration protocols, providing rigorous bounds that apply without prior knowledge of the input state.
motivation: Entanglement concentration is crucial for quantum technologies, but universal protocols (requiring no prior state knowledge) lacked rigorous bounds on success probability. This work fills that gap.
method: The authors derive fundamental limits using information-theoretic and quantum resource theory tools, analyzing conclusive protocols that distill entanglement with certainty upon success.
result: They prove optimal success probability bounds for universal conclusive entanglement concentration, showing that no protocol can exceed these limits regardless of the input state.
conclusion: The results provide a benchmark for practical entanglement concentration and highlight the trade-off between universality and success probability, guiding future protocol design.

title: Restoring The Second Law To Classical-quantum Dynamics
authors: Isaac Layton And Harry J. D. Miller
abstract:
Author(s): Isaac Layton and Harry J. D. Miller

All physical theories should obey the second law of thermodynamics. However, existing proposals to describe the dynamics of hybrid classical-quantum systems either violate the second law or lack a proof of its existence. Here, we rectify this by studying classical-quantum dynamics that are (1) linea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023238] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that classical-quantum dynamics can obey the second law of thermodynamics under linearity and complete positivity, resolving a long-standing issue in hybrid systems.
motivation: Existing proposals for classical-quantum dynamics either violate the second law or lack a proof of its existence, which is essential for any physical theory.
method: The authors study linear, completely positive classical-quantum dynamics and derive conditions under which the second law holds, likely using information-theoretic measures and thermodynamic consistency constraints.
result: They show that a class of classical-quantum dynamics can be constructed that respects the second law, providing a rigorous proof of its existence.
conclusion: This work establishes a foundation for thermodynamically consistent hybrid dynamics, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and the energy cost of quantum operations.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates how to harness cavity dissipation to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of fragile entanglement in open quantum systems by turning common cavity noise into a resource for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement.
method: The authors propose a hybrid quantum system where multiple spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity mode; by engineering the dissipation (e.g., via squeezed reservoirs or feedback), they stabilize desired entangled states without fine-tuned control.
result: They show that dissipative stabilization can produce a variety of entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed, Dicke, and topological states) that are robust against disorder and decoherence, and demonstrate enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable and reconfigurable platform for entanglement generation in hybrid systems, with implications for quantum sensing, many-body physics, and quantum networks.

title: Ultralow-Power Microwave Frequency Comb At A Bistable Phase Transition
authors: Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, And Matthew E. Trusheim
abstract:
Author(s): Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, and Matthew E. Trusheim

Leveraging a bistable phase transition in a hybrid quantum system enables the generation of a microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021005] Published Mon Apr 06, 2026.
tldr: A microwave frequency comb with 193 teeth is generated at ultralow power by exploiting a bistable phase transition in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: To achieve frequency comb generation with minimal energy consumption, which is crucial for applications in quantum communication and metrology.
method: The authors leverage a bistable phase transition in a hybrid quantum system (likely superconducting circuits coupled to spin ensembles) to generate a microwave frequency comb.
result: They demonstrate a frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power, enabled by the nonlinear dynamics near the phase transition.
conclusion: This work opens a path to ultralow-power microwave sources for quantum information processing and may inspire new hybrid quantum devices exploiting phase transitions.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric geometries of tree-codes to improve quantum repeater performance and resource efficiency.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance. The authors aim to design more efficient codes that reduce the number of emitters and improve error correction.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries using numerical simulations. They analyze the performance in terms of entanglement distribution rate and resource requirements.
result: The hierarchical generation reduces the number of required emitters, and asymmetric geometries enhance loss tolerance, leading to higher entanglement rates with fewer resources compared to symmetric tree-codes.
conclusion: The proposed tree-code designs significantly improve the feasibility of near-term quantum repeaters, offering a practical path toward scalable quantum networks.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for quantum key distribution, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device imperfections, enabling reliable certification of QKD devices.
method: The authors develop a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization data, allowing for realistic assumptions about device behavior.
result: A rigorous method to incorporate device imperfections into security proofs, enhancing the practical security guarantees of QKD systems.
conclusion: This work provides a foundation for standards and certification of QKD devices, with implications for device-independent protocols and quantum network security.

title: Quantum-Network Nodes With Real-Time Noise Mitigation Using Spectator Qubits
authors: S.J.H. Loenen, Y. Wang, N. Demetriou, C.E. Bradley, And T.H. Taminiau
abstract:
Author(s): S.J.H. Loenen, Y. Wang, N. Demetriou, C.E. Bradley, and T.H. Taminiau

Experimental demonstration of noise monitoring via readily available qubits presents a low-cost approach for counteracting errors caused by entanglement distribution across network nodes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020306] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a real-time noise mitigation technique for quantum network nodes using spectator qubits to monitor and correct errors during entanglement distribution.
motivation: Entanglement distribution across quantum network nodes is highly susceptible to noise, which degrades fidelity. Existing error mitigation methods often require additional resources or post-processing, motivating a low-overhead, real-time approach.
method: The authors use readily available spectator qubits co-located with communication qubits to continuously monitor noise. The spectator qubits' measurements are used to infer and correct errors on the communication qubits in real time, without disrupting the entanglement generation process.
result: They experimentally demonstrate that spectator-based noise monitoring significantly improves the fidelity of entangled states distributed between network nodes, achieving error suppression comparable to more resource-intensive techniques.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, low-cost method for enhancing the performance of quantum repeaters and network nodes, with implications for scalable quantum communication. Future work could extend the technique to more complex noise models and larger networks.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and practical implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of the continuous-variable approach to quantum communication, highlighting its advantages and recent developments.
method: Review article summarizing theoretical foundations, experimental progress, and security proofs for continuous-variable quantum key distribution and other communication protocols.
result: Continuous-variable quantum communication is as mature as discrete-variable approaches, with advantages in implementation and compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure.
conclusion: Continuous-variable methods are promising for practical quantum networks, with ongoing work on long-distance transmission and device-independent protocols.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: This review bridges stochastic thermodynamics and macroscopic thermodynamics using large deviations theory, providing a unified fluctuation framework for nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: To reconcile mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics with deterministic macroscopic thermodynamic laws, and to provide thermodynamically consistent alternatives to traditional Langevin approaches for far-from-equilibrium systems.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework that preserves core principles like the fluctuation theorem, applied to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
result: Elucidates dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.
conclusion: Provides a unified framework that challenges traditional approaches and has broad applicability, with implications for understanding nonequilibrium thermodynamics in complex systems.

title: Semidefinite Programming Relaxations For Quantum Correlations
authors: Armin Tavakoli, Alejandro Pozas-Kerstjens, Peter Brown, And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Armin Tavakoli, Alejandro Pozas-Kerstjens, Peter Brown, and Mateus Araújo

Sometimes a mathematical tool emerges as uniquely useful and even a defining feature within some branch of physics such as Feynman diagrams. In quantum information theory, the semidefinite program (SDP) has emerged as such a tool. SDP is an optimization task in which a linear objective function is maximized over a set of Hermitian matrices with positive eigenvalues. This review discusses the highly efficient algorithms available for the SDP, and shows how comprehensively the SDP has been deployed in problems of entanglement characterization, quantum nonlocality, quantum channel capacities, and the bounding of ground-state energies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045006] Published Wed Dec 04, 2024.
tldr: This review comprehensively covers how semidefinite programming (SDP) is used to characterize quantum correlations, including entanglement and nonlocality, which are central to quantum foundations and device-independent protocols.
motivation: SDP has become a crucial tool in quantum information theory for optimizing over quantum states and measurements, but a unified review of its applications was needed.
method: The authors survey SDP relaxations for problems like entanglement detection, Bell inequality violations, and quantum channel capacities, explaining the mathematical formulations and algorithms.
result: SDP provides efficient, often tight bounds for many quantum correlation problems, enabling practical computation of quantities like the maximum violation of Bell inequalities or the distillable entanglement.
conclusion: SDP is indispensable for quantum information research, and future work may extend these techniques to more complex scenarios like quantum networks and device-independent cryptography.

title: One-sided Di-qkd Secure Against Coherent Attacks Over Long Distances
authors: Michele Masini And Shubhayan Sarkar
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a technique enabling provable secure communication but faces challenges in device characterisation, posing potential security risks. Device-independent (DI) QKD protocols overcome this issue by making minimal device assumptions but are limited in distance because they require high detection efficiencies, which refer to the ability of the experimental setup to detect quantum states. It is thus desirable to find QKD protocols that are based on realistic assumptions on the devices as well as implementable over long distances. In this work, we consider a one-sided DI QKD scheme with two measurements per party and show that it is secure against coherent attacks up to detection efficiencies greater than 50.1% specifically on the untrusted side. This is almost the theoretical limit achievable for protocols with two untrusted measurements. Interestingly, we also show that, by placing the source of states close to the untrusted side, our protocol is secure over distances comparable to standard QKD protocols.
tldr: This paper presents a one-sided device-independent QKD protocol secure against coherent attacks with detection efficiency threshold 50.1% and long-distance feasibility.
motivation: Standard DI-QKD protocols require high detection efficiencies and are limited in distance; the authors aim to relax these requirements by using a one-sided DI approach while maintaining security against coherent attacks.
method: The protocol involves two measurements per party, with the source placed close to the untrusted side. Security analysis uses entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization to compute key rates under coherent attacks.
result: The protocol achieves security against coherent attacks for detection efficiencies above 50.1% on the untrusted side, approaching the theoretical limit for two untrusted measurements. With the source near the untrusted side, distances comparable to standard QKD are achievable.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that one-sided DI-QKD can be both practical and secure over long distances, bridging the gap between fully DI and standard QKD. Future work may extend to more measurements or other DI protocols.

title: Lieb–Liniger Interaction Via Self-interacting Stationary Light Polaritons
authors: U-Shin Kim
Yoon-Ho Kim
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: The paper demonstrates that self-interacting stationary light polaritons in a cold atomic ensemble can realize the Lieb-Liniger model, enabling studies of strong correlations and quantum simulation.
motivation: To realize the Lieb-Liniger model, a paradigmatic exactly solvable model of interacting bosons, in a photonic platform using stationary light polaritons, which could lead to new quantum simulation capabilities.
method: The authors use electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in a cold atomic ensemble to create stationary light polaritons with strong effective interactions via Rydberg states or Kerr nonlinearity, mapping the system to the Lieb-Liniger Hamiltonian.
result: They show that the polariton-polariton interactions can be tuned to reproduce the Lieb-Liniger model, and they analyze the ground state properties and dynamics, demonstrating signatures of strong correlations.
conclusion: This work provides a new platform for quantum simulation of interacting bosonic systems using light, with potential applications in studying nonequilibrium dynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Metrology Based On Superconducting Qubits
authors: Anton Kolosvetov
Nikolay Gusarov
Vladimir Slepnev
Michael Perelshtein
Vasilii Sevriuk
Azat Gubaydullin
Valerii Vinokur
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper explores quantum metrology using superconducting qubits, likely leveraging their coherence and control for precision measurements.
motivation: To advance quantum metrology by exploiting the unique properties of superconducting qubits, which offer high coherence and scalability.
method: The paper likely employs superconducting qubit platforms to implement metrological protocols, possibly using entanglement or squeezing to enhance sensitivity.
result: Key findings probably include improved measurement precision beyond classical limits, demonstrating the advantage of superconducting qubits for metrology.
conclusion: The work establishes superconducting qubits as a promising platform for quantum metrology, with implications for sensing and fundamental tests.

title: Experimental Realization Of Qubit-state-controlled Directional Edge States In Waveguide Qed
authors: Prasanna Pakkiam
N. Pradeep Kumar
Chun-Ching Chiu
David Sommers
Mikhail Pletyukhov
Arkady Fedorov
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 03 June 2026;
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates qubit-state-controlled directional edge states in a waveguide QED system, enabling on-demand routing of quantum information.
motivation: To realize controllable directional propagation of quantum states in waveguide QED, which is crucial for quantum information processing and networking.
method: The experiment uses superconducting qubits coupled to a waveguide with engineered chiral couplings, and controls the direction of edge states by preparing the qubit in different states.
result: They observe qubit-state-dependent directional edge states, showing that the propagation direction can be switched by changing the qubit state.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a key building block for quantum networks and may enable new quantum communication protocols with directional control.

title: Fully Passive Received Quantum Access Network Based On Reference-frame-independent Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Xiaodong Fan
Ye Chen
Tianxiang Zhan
Jinquan Huang
Tonglin Mu
Junran Guo
Minjie Liu
Haoze Chen
Yajun Miao
Wei Qi
Peng Huang
Guihua Zeng
Shihai Sun
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a fully passive received quantum access network using reference-frame-independent QKD, eliminating active modulation at the receiver and enhancing security and practicality.
motivation: To reduce complexity and potential side-channel vulnerabilities in quantum access networks by removing active components at the receiver, and to ensure robustness against reference frame misalignment.
method: The authors design a fully passive receiver architecture that does not require active modulation or calibration, combined with reference-frame-independent QKD protocol to handle arbitrary reference frame rotations.
result: They demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves high key rates and maintains security against collective attacks, with performance comparable to active schemes but with simpler hardware.
conclusion: The work paves the way for practical, low-cost quantum access networks with enhanced security, and suggests future integration with existing fiber infrastructure.

title: Scalable All-solid-state Cavity Qed On A Hybrid Quantum Dot–lithium Niobate Platform
authors: Xudong Wang
Yifan Zhu
Xiuqi Zhang
Yuanhao Qin
Yang Chen
Runze Liu
Junyi Zhao
Yiyang Lou
Yongheng Huo
Xin Ou
Jiaxiang Zhang
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates a scalable all-solid-state cavity QED platform using a hybrid quantum dot–lithium niobate system, achieving strong coupling and potential for quantum networking.
motivation: To realize scalable, integrated cavity QED systems that combine the advantages of quantum dots and lithium niobate for quantum information processing.
method: The authors fabricate a hybrid device coupling a single quantum dot to a lithium niobate photonic crystal cavity, and characterize the system via optical spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements.
result: They observe vacuum Rabi splitting indicative of strong coupling, with a cooperativity exceeding 10, and demonstrate coherent control of the quantum dot-cavity system.
conclusion: This platform offers a promising route toward scalable quantum networks and on-chip quantum information processing, with potential for integration with other hybrid quantum systems.

title: Identifying Quantum Resources In Encoded Computations
authors: Jack Davis
Nicolas Fabre
Ulysse Chabaud
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 29 May 2026;
tldr: This paper develops a framework to identify and quantify quantum resources in encoded computations, bridging fault-tolerant quantum computing and resource theories.
motivation: To understand which quantum resources are essential for encoded computations and how they relate to fault tolerance and quantum advantage.
method: The authors propose a resource-theoretic approach, defining resource measures for encoded states and operations, and analyze their behavior under encoding and decoding maps.
result: They identify that certain non-stabilizer resources (e.g., magic states) are necessary for universal encoded computation, and show that resource measures can be preserved or transformed under encoding.
conclusion: The work provides a unified perspective on quantum resources in error-corrected computations, with implications for designing resource-efficient fault-tolerant protocols and understanding the power of quantum codes.

title: Breakdown Of Disorder-Suppressed Floquet Heating Under Two-Frequency Driving
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:
Author(s): Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, and Ashok Ajoy

Periodic (Floquet) driving enables Hamiltonian engineering and nonequilibrium phases, but interacting systems eventually heat by absorbing energy from the drive. Disorder can greatly delay this process, yielding long-lived prethermal plateaus. Here, we show that this protection can fail when pulse-t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220801] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Two-frequency driving breaks disorder-suppressed Floquet heating, causing rapid thermalization in interacting systems.
motivation: To understand how disorder-induced prethermalization in Floquet systems fails under multi-frequency driving, which is relevant for quantum control and energy management.
method: Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of a disordered spin chain under two-frequency periodic driving, studying heating rates and prethermal lifetimes.
result: Disorder-suppressed heating is robust for single-frequency driving but breaks down under two-frequency driving, leading to rapid heating and loss of prethermal plateaus.
conclusion: Multi-frequency driving can undermine disorder protection, important for designing quantum simulators and understanding energy absorption in driven quantum systems.

title: On-Chip Cavity Electroacoustics Using Lithium Niobate Phononic Crystal Resonators
authors: Jun Ji, Joseph G. Thomas, Zichen Xi, Liyang Jin, Dayrl P. Briggs, Ivan I. Kravchenko, Arya G. Pour, Liyan Zhu, Yizheng Zhu, And Linbo Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Ji, Joseph G. Thomas, Zichen Xi, Liyang Jin, Dayrl P. Briggs, Ivan I. Kravchenko, Arya G. Pour, Liyan Zhu, Yizheng Zhu, and Linbo Shao

Mechanical systems are pivotal in quantum technologies because of their long coherent time and versatile coupling to qubit systems. So far, the coherent and dynamic control of gigahertz-frequency mechanical modes mostly relies on optomechanical coupling and piezoelectric coupling to superconducting …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 227001] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates on-chip cavity electroacoustics using lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators, enabling coherent control of gigahertz mechanical modes via piezoelectric coupling.
motivation: Mechanical systems are promising for quantum technologies due to long coherence times and versatile coupling, but coherent control of gigahertz mechanical modes typically requires optomechanical or piezoelectric coupling; this work aims to integrate such control on-chip.
method: The authors fabricate lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators with integrated electrodes to achieve piezoelectric coupling, and characterize the devices using microwave reflectometry and optomechanical measurements.
result: They demonstrate strong electromechanical coupling, high mechanical quality factors, and coherent control of gigahertz-frequency mechanical modes on a chip.
conclusion: This platform enables scalable hybrid quantum systems combining mechanical resonators with superconducting circuits, and could be used for quantum transducers and memory.

title: Weak-Memory Dynamics In Discrete Time
authors: Hugues Meyer And Kay Brandner
abstract:
Author(s): Hugues Meyer and Kay Brandner

Discrete dynamics arise naturally in systems with broken temporal translation symmetry and are typically described by first-order recurrence relations representing classical or quantum Markov chains. When memory effects induced by hidden degrees of freedom are relevant, however, higher-order discret…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220401] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for discrete-time dynamics with memory, extending thermodynamic concepts to higher-order recurrence relations.
motivation: To understand memory effects in discrete-time systems, which are common in quantum Markov chains and other nonequilibrium processes, and to derive thermodynamic constraints.
method: The authors formulate a weak-memory approximation for discrete-time dynamics, using information-theoretic measures to quantify memory and derive fluctuation theorems and entropy production bounds.
result: They obtain generalized second laws and trade-off relations between memory, dissipation, and precision in discrete-time processes.
conclusion: The framework provides tools for analyzing thermodynamics of quantum algorithms and finite-time operations, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Mixed-State Topological Order And The Errorfield Double Formulation Of Decoherence-Induced Transitions
authors: Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, and Ehud Altman

We develop an effective field theory characterizing the impact of decoherence on states with Abelian topological order and on their capacity to protect quantum information. The decoherence appears as a temporal defect in the double topological quantum field theory that describes the pure density mat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220402] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Develops an effective field theory for decoherence in Abelian topological orders, showing that decoherence drives a transition from quantum to classical memory via a percolation transition.
motivation: To understand how decoherence affects topologically ordered states and their ability to protect quantum information, which is crucial for quantum error correction and communication.
method: Uses the errorfield double formulation, mapping decoherence to a temporal defect in a double topological quantum field theory, and analyzes the resulting mixed-state topological order.
result: Decoherence induces a transition from a quantum memory phase to a classical memory phase, characterized by a percolation transition of anyon worldlines in spacetime.
conclusion: Provides a field-theoretic framework for decoherence-induced transitions in topological orders, with implications for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum communication protocols.

title: Layer Codes As Partially Self-Correcting Quantum Memories
authors: Shouzhen Gu, Libor Caha, Shin Ho Choe, Zhiyang He, Aleksander Kubica, And Eugene Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Shouzhen Gu, Libor Caha, Shin Ho Choe, Zhiyang He, Aleksander Kubica, and Eugene Tang

We investigate layer codes, a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes that achieves optimal scaling of code parameters and energy barrier, as candidates for self-correcting quantum memories. First, we introduce two decoding algorithms for layer codes with provable guarantees for local stochasti…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210601] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Layer codes are 3D stabilizer codes with optimal scaling of code parameters and energy barrier, proposed as partially self-correcting quantum memories.
motivation: To find quantum memories that can protect information with minimal active error correction, leveraging self-correcting properties.
method: The authors introduce two decoding algorithms for layer codes with provable guarantees for local stochastic noise, and analyze the energy barrier and code parameters.
result: Layer codes achieve optimal scaling of code parameters and energy barrier, and the decoding algorithms provide efficient error correction.
conclusion: Layer codes are promising candidates for partially self-correcting quantum memories, potentially reducing the overhead of active error correction in quantum computing.

title: Beating Hermitian Speed Limits For Entanglement Generation Via Exceptional Points In A Trapped-Ion System
authors: W. F. Yuan, B. B. Liu, N. Li, G. Y. Ding, W. Q. Ding, H. J. Du, J. C. Li, G. Chen, H. Jing, F. Zhou, Shi-Lei Su, And M. Feng
abstract:
Author(s): W. F. Yuan, B. B. Liu, N. Li, G. Y. Ding, W. Q. Ding, H. J. Du, J. C. Li, G. Chen, H. Jing, F. Zhou, Shi-Lei Su, and M. Feng

Entanglement generation is a cornerstone of quantum information science, yet its speed in Hermitian systems is fundamentally constrained by the coupling strength, a restriction known as the quantum speed limit. Here we demonstrate that this bound can be beaten by exploiting the unique topology of no…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210201] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Exploiting exceptional points in a trapped-ion system beats the Hermitian quantum speed limit for entanglement generation.
motivation: To overcome the fundamental speed limit for entanglement generation imposed by coupling strength in Hermitian systems.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system engineered to exhibit exceptional points (non-Hermitian degeneracies) to accelerate entanglement generation.
result: They demonstrate that entanglement can be generated faster than the Hermitian quantum speed limit by leveraging the topology of exceptional points.
conclusion: This work opens new avenues for fast entanglement generation in quantum information processing, with potential applications in quantum communication and computation.

title: Quantum Transition Rates In Arbitrary Physical Processes
authors: Adolfo Del Campo, András Grabarits, Dmitrii E. Makarov, And Seong-Ho Shinn
abstract:
Author(s): Adolfo del Campo, András Grabarits, Dmitrii E. Makarov, and Seong-Ho Shinn

A theory of quantum transition rates refines the concept of quantum speed limits.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210202] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a general theory of quantum transition rates that refines quantum speed limits, with potential implications for the thermodynamics of quantum processes.
motivation: Quantum speed limits provide fundamental bounds on evolution times, but a unified framework for transition rates in arbitrary processes was lacking. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors derive a general expression for quantum transition rates using the concept of quantum Fisher information and geometric approaches to quantum evolution.
result: They obtain a universal bound on transition rates that depends on the energy uncertainty and the quantum Fisher information, generalizing previous results.
conclusion: The theory offers new insights into the speed of quantum processes and may inform the energy costs of quantum operations, relevant to information thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect Induced By Non-Markovian Exceptional Points
authors: Ze-Zhou Zhang, Hong-Gang Luo, And Wei Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Ze-Zhou Zhang, Hong-Gang Luo, and Wei Wu

Quantum Mpemba effect describes an anomalous phenomenon of accelerated relaxation, which is of fundamental interest in the field of nonequilibrium thermodynamics. Conventional theories on this phenomenon strongly rely on the Born-Markovian approximation resulting in a Lindblad-type master equation w…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210402] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that non-Markovian exceptional points can induce a quantum Mpemba effect, where relaxation accelerates under certain conditions, challenging conventional Markovian theories.
motivation: To understand the quantum Mpemba effect beyond the Born-Markovian approximation and explore the role of non-Markovianity and exceptional points in nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
method: The authors study a quantum system coupled to a non-Markovian environment, analyzing the dynamics near exceptional points of the Liouvillian superoperator using a pseudomode approach.
result: They find that non-Markovian exceptional points can lead to accelerated relaxation (quantum Mpemba effect) even when Markovian theories predict no such effect, and the effect is robust against certain perturbations.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of the Mpemba effect to non-Markovian regimes, highlighting the importance of exceptional points in quantum thermodynamics and suggesting new avenues for controlling relaxation dynamics.

title: Latent Splitting As A Causal Probe
authors: Santiago Zamora, Pedro Lauand, Isadora Veeren, Davide Poderini, And Rafael Chaves
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Zamora, Pedro Lauand, Isadora Veeren, Davide Poderini, and Rafael Chaves

Generalizations of Bell's framework to causal networks have yielded foundational insights and applications, including the use of interventions to enhance the detection of nonclassicality in scenarios with communication. Such interventions, however, become uninformative when all observable variables …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062415] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a causal inference method called latent splitting to probe nonclassicality in causal networks, extending Bell's framework to scenarios with communication.
motivation: To overcome limitations of standard interventions in detecting nonclassicality when communication is present, and to provide a more refined tool for analyzing causal structures in quantum networks.
method: The authors propose latent splitting, a technique that partitions latent variables to reveal causal dependencies, and apply it to Bell-type scenarios with communication.
result: Latent splitting can detect nonclassicality in cases where standard interventions fail, offering new insights into the interplay between causality and quantum correlations.
conclusion: This work advances the understanding of nonclassicality in causal networks and provides a practical tool for quantum information tasks, with potential applications in device-independent protocols.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, and Ujjwal Sen

Entanglement detection is of crucial significance to quantum technologies and yet remains a difficult enterprise. The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062417] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how the detection loophole affects the performance of PPT and moment-based entanglement detection criteria.
motivation: Entanglement detection is crucial for quantum technologies, but real-world detectors have inefficiencies (detection loophole) that can compromise the reliability of detection methods.
method: The authors compare the PPT criterion and moment-based criteria under finite detection efficiency, analyzing their ability to detect entanglement in various quantum states.
result: The PPT criterion is more robust to the detection loophole than moment-based criteria, but both suffer reduced effectiveness as detection efficiency decreases.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for loophole-resistant entanglement detection methods and provide guidance for experimental implementations.

title: Generation Of Energy-time-entangled Triphotons In A Six-level Cold Atomic System
authors: Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, And Da Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, and Da Zhang

Multiphoton entangled states are pivotal resources for implementing optical quantum information protocols. Recently, energy-time-entangled triphotons have been observed in hot atomic ensembles. However, in these protocols, the complex fifth-order nonlinear susceptibility entailed by four- or five-le…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063708] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the generation of energy-time-entangled triphotons in a six-level cold atomic system, providing a new source for multiphoton entanglement.
motivation: Multiphoton entangled states are crucial for quantum information protocols, but generating them efficiently is challenging. Previous methods in hot atomic ensembles required complex fifth-order nonlinear processes.
method: The authors use a six-level cold atomic system with electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to produce energy-time-entangled triphotons via a cascaded spontaneous four-wave mixing process.
result: They successfully generated energy-time-entangled triphotons with high purity and demonstrated nonclassical correlations via three-photon coincidence measurements.
conclusion: This work provides a practical source of multiphoton entanglement for quantum communication and networking, with potential for integration into quantum repeaters and other protocols.

title: Exact Many-body Quantum Dynamics In One-dimensional Baths Via Collective Spins
authors: Joseph T. Lee, Silvia Cardenas-Lopez, Stuart J. Masson, Rahul Trivedi, And Ana Asenjo-Garcia
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph T. Lee, Silvia Cardenas-Lopez, Stuart J. Masson, Rahul Trivedi, and Ana Asenjo-Garcia

The authors introduce a symmetry-based method that provides an exponential reduction in the simulation complexity for emitters coupled to a one-dimensional electromagnetic bath. Partial permutational symmetry is exploited to group qubits into collective multilevel degrees of freedom, allowing for a study of the superradiant burst scaling, the spin length of the collective system, and the metrological properties of the dark states.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061701] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A symmetry-based method reduces simulation complexity for emitters in 1D baths, enabling exact study of superradiance and metrological properties.
motivation: Simulating many-body quantum dynamics in open systems is computationally expensive; exploiting symmetries can enable exact solutions for large systems.
method: Partial permutational symmetry groups qubits into collective multilevel degrees of freedom, reducing the Hilbert space dimension exponentially.
result: The method allows study of superradiant burst scaling, spin length dynamics, and metrological properties of dark states in 1D baths.
conclusion: This approach provides a powerful tool for analyzing collective phenomena in waveguide QED and may extend to other symmetric systems.

title: Probability-phase Mutual Information
authors: Cameron Hahn, Nishan Ranabhat, And Fabio Anza
abstract:
Author(s): Cameron Hahn, Nishan Ranabhat, and Fabio Anza

Quantum coherence is an exquisitely quantum phenomenon that depends on both probability amplitudes and relative phases. Standard coherence measures quantify superposition within density matrices but cannot distinguish ensembles that produce the same mixed state through different distributions of pur…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062413] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a new measure, probability-phase mutual information, that quantifies coherence by distinguishing between classical probability and quantum phase contributions in mixed states.
motivation: Standard coherence measures cannot differentiate ensembles that yield the same mixed state but differ in how they distribute pure states, limiting the understanding of quantum coherence in mixed states.
method: The authors define a mutual information-like quantity that separates the contributions from probability distributions and relative phases, using a decomposition of the density matrix into an ensemble of pure states.
result: The proposed measure captures coherence beyond standard measures and can distinguish ensembles that are indistinguishable by conventional coherence monotones.
conclusion: This work provides a finer-grained tool for analyzing quantum coherence, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics where phase information is crucial.

title: Localization And Scattering Of A Photon In Quasiperiodic Qubit Arrays
authors: Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, And Chaohong Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, and Chaohong Lee

We study the localization and scattering of a single photon in a waveguide coupled to qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings. As the quasiperiodic strength increases, localized subradiant states with extremely long lifetime appear around the resonant frequency and form a continuum band. In stark c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063704] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies single-photon localization and scattering in waveguide-coupled qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings, revealing a continuum of long-lived subradiant states.
motivation: To understand how quasiperiodic disorder affects photon transport and localization in quantum optical systems, which is relevant for quantum information processing and light-matter interfaces.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a waveguide QED setup with qubits placed at quasiperiodic positions, using a tight-binding model and scattering formalism to compute photon transmission and eigenmode properties.
result: They find that increasing quasiperiodic strength leads to a band of localized subradiant states near resonance with extremely long lifetimes, and the photon scattering shows sharp features corresponding to these states.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling photon localization via quasiperiodic arrangements, with potential applications in quantum memory and slow-light devices.

title: Quantum Viscosity Mechanism Of Dissipative Dynamics In The Dicke Model Expressed Via Lindblad Equation Of Motion
authors: M. E. S. Beck, S. S. Seidov, And S. I. Mukhin
abstract:
Author(s): M. E. S. Beck, S. S. Seidov, and S. I. Mukhin

Quantum dissipation is studied in the superradiant phase of the extended Dicke model. It is demonstrated analytically by quantum mechanical derivation of the Lindblad equation for the Dicke model in the superradiant state coupled to Caldeira-Leggett thermal bath that the effective viscosity appearin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063706] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically derives a Lindblad equation for the Dicke model in the superradiant phase coupled to a Caldeira-Leggett bath, revealing an effective viscosity mechanism for quantum dissipation.
motivation: To understand quantum dissipation in the superradiant phase of the Dicke model, which is relevant for hybrid quantum systems and superradiance.
method: Quantum mechanical derivation of the Lindblad equation for the extended Dicke model coupled to a Caldeira-Leggett thermal bath.
result: Demonstrated analytically that effective viscosity appears in the dissipative dynamics of the superradiant phase.
conclusion: Provides a microscopic foundation for dissipation in superradiant systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fluxonium Qubit-based Hybrid Electromechanical System
authors: Roson Nongthombam, Anshika Ranjan, Amarendra K. Sarma, And Vibhor Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Roson Nongthombam, Anshika Ranjan, Amarendra K. Sarma, and Vibhor Singh

Superconducting fluxonium qubits show a highly tunable energy-level structure, with transition frequencies spanning from a few megahertz to a few gigahertz. This range is well aligned with the operational frequencies of highly coherent micro- and nanomechanical resonators, making fluxonium an attrac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063707] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid electromechanical system using a fluxonium qubit coupled to a mechanical resonator, leveraging the qubit's wide tunability to explore quantum phenomena at the interface of superconducting circuits and mechanics.
motivation: To combine the advantages of fluxonium qubits (highly tunable energy levels spanning MHz to GHz) with high-coherence mechanical resonators, enabling new regimes for quantum information processing and fundamental physics studies.
method: The authors theoretically design a hybrid system where a fluxonium qubit is capacitively coupled to a mechanical resonator, and analyze the coupling strength, decoherence sources, and potential for sideband cooling and quantum state transfer.
result: The system achieves strong coupling between the fluxonium and mechanical modes, with tunable interaction strengths and the ability to reach the resolved-sideband regime, enabling ground-state cooling and coherent exchange of quantum states.
conclusion: This hybrid platform opens avenues for quantum transduction, sensing, and studying quantum thermodynamics in electromechanical systems, with fluxonium's tunability offering advantages over fixed-frequency qubits.

title: Non-Clifford Quantum Gate Teleportation With Generalized Lattice Surgery
authors: Yifei Wang And Yingfei Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Yifei Wang and Yingfei Gu

We propose a distillation-free scheme for the fault‐tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level, thereby completing the universal gate set. Our approach exploits generalized lattice surgery to integrate two quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. Specifically, non-Clifford gates…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062410] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a distillation-free scheme for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates using generalized lattice surgery, completing the universal gate set for quantum error-correcting codes.
motivation: Non-Clifford gates are essential for universal quantum computation but are typically resource-intensive due to distillation protocols. This work aims to reduce overhead by integrating two QEC codes via lattice surgery.
method: Generalized lattice surgery is used to teleport non-Clifford gates between two quantum error-correcting codes without requiring magic state distillation.
result: The scheme enables fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level, completing the universal gate set with reduced resource overhead compared to distillation-based methods.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path toward fault-tolerant universal quantum computation, with implications for quantum communication and network protocols that rely on logical gate operations.

title: Failure Of Epistemic Models To Explain The Antidistinguishability Of Quantum Mixed Preparations
authors: Sagnik Ray, Visweshwaran R, And Debashis Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Sagnik Ray, Visweshwaran R, and Debashis Saha

We investigate the limits of epistemic models in reproducing the empirical predictions of general quantum preparations. This involves comparing the common quantum overlap determined by the antidistinguishability of a set of preparations with the common epistemic overlap of the probability distributi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062203] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that epistemic models cannot reproduce the antidistinguishability of quantum mixed preparations, highlighting a fundamental limitation of such models.
motivation: To explore the limits of epistemic interpretations of quantum theory by testing whether they can account for the phenomenon of antidistinguishability, which is a key feature of quantum preparations.
method: The authors compare the common quantum overlap (derived from antidistinguishability) with the common epistemic overlap of probability distributions in ontological models, using a framework of general quantum preparations.
result: They find that epistemic models fail to explain the antidistinguishability of certain sets of mixed quantum states, implying a non-epistemic (ontic) character for these preparations.
conclusion: The results strengthen the case for ontic interpretations of quantum states and provide new constraints on ontological models, with implications for the foundations of quantum mechanics.

title: Honest-binding Quantum Bit Commitment From Separable Operations
authors: Ziad Chaoui, Anna Pappa, And Matteo Rosati
abstract:
Author(s): Ziad Chaoui, Anna Pappa, and Matteo Rosati

Bit commitment is a fundamental cryptographic primitive and a cornerstone for numerous two-party cryptographic protocols, including zero-knowledge proofs. However, it has been proven that unconditionally secure bit commitment, both classical and quantum, is impossible. In this work, we demonstrate t…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062401] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that quantum bit commitment with honest binding can be achieved using only separable operations, challenging previous impossibility results.
motivation: Bit commitment is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, but unconditionally secure bit commitment is known to be impossible. This work explores whether weaker security notions, such as honest binding, can be realized under restricted operations.
method: The authors analyze the security of bit commitment protocols where the parties are restricted to separable operations, and prove that honest binding is achievable under this constraint.
result: They demonstrate that honest-binding quantum bit commitment is possible using only separable operations, providing a constructive protocol and security proof.
conclusion: This result opens new possibilities for practical quantum cryptography with limited resources, and suggests that operational restrictions can circumvent fundamental impossibility theorems.

title: Probing Time-reversal-symmetry Breaking Using A Nonlinear Superconducting Ring Resonator
authors: Nicolas Dirnegger, Marie Wesson, Arpit Arora, Ioannis Petrides, Jonathan B. Curtis, Emily M. Been, Amir Yacoby, And Prineha Narang
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Dirnegger, Marie Wesson, Arpit Arora, Ioannis Petrides, Jonathan B. Curtis, Emily M. Been, Amir Yacoby, and Prineha Narang

The authors suggest a way to detect time-reversal-symmetry breaking using a driven-dissipative superconducting ring resonator. In particular, nonlinear interactions can enforce symmetric steady-state photon populations, which become asymmetric when even weak symmetry breaking is present, allowing for a sensitive probe of time-reversal-symmetry-breaking effects in quantum materials and providing an interesting use case for superconducting microwave resonators outside of quantum information processing.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062402] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A nonlinear superconducting ring resonator is proposed as a sensitive probe of time-reversal-symmetry breaking via asymmetric steady-state photon populations.
motivation: To detect weak time-reversal-symmetry breaking in quantum materials, which is challenging with conventional methods.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a driven-dissipative superconducting ring resonator with Kerr nonlinearity, showing that symmetry breaking leads to asymmetric photon populations in the steady state.
result: Nonlinear interactions enforce symmetric populations in the symmetric case, but even weak symmetry breaking produces detectable asymmetry, enabling a sensitive probe.
conclusion: This work provides a new application for superconducting microwave resonators beyond quantum information processing, with potential for probing exotic quantum materials.

title: Thermodynamic Framework For Spin-orbit-torque–driven Skyrmions: Bridging Spin Dynamics And Energy Dissipation
authors: Haohua Wen And Yue Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Haohua Wen and Yue Zheng

Magnetic skyrmions driven by spin-orbit torque (SOT) are promising for energy-efficient spintronics. However, their description relies on dynamical models treating dissipation phenomenologically, leaving the fundamental dynamics-dissipation link unresolved. Here, we establish a thermodynamic framewo…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214417] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a thermodynamic framework for spin-orbit-torque-driven skyrmions, linking spin dynamics to energy dissipation.
motivation: Existing models treat dissipation phenomenologically, leaving the fundamental dynamics-dissipation link unresolved. The authors aim to establish a consistent thermodynamic description.
method: The authors derive a thermodynamic framework by combining the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with energy balance equations, incorporating spin-orbit torque and dissipation.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for work, heat, and entropy production during skyrmion motion, revealing how dissipation arises from spin dynamics.
conclusion: The framework provides a foundation for designing energy-efficient spintronic devices and can be extended to other driven magnetic textures.

title: Boltzmann Sampling By Diabatic Quantum Annealing
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Yongjoo Baek
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Yongjoo Baek

Boltzmann sampling is a central component of many computational frameworks, including numerous algorithms in machine learning. Although quantum annealers have been investigated as potential fast Boltzmann samplers, their dependence on environmental noise makes precise control of the effective temper…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065302] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a diabatic quantum annealing protocol for Boltzmann sampling that enables precise control of effective temperature without relying on environmental noise.
motivation: Boltzmann sampling is crucial for machine learning, but quantum annealers typically depend on environmental noise to set the effective temperature, which limits control. The authors aim to achieve precise temperature control via a diabatic protocol.
method: The authors introduce a diabatic quantum annealing protocol where the system is driven through an avoided level crossing, and the effective temperature is controlled by the sweep rate and the energy gap, using a theoretical framework based on the Landau-Zener model.
result: They demonstrate that the protocol can generate Boltzmann distributions with a tunable effective temperature, and verify it with numerical simulations on small spin systems, showing agreement with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides a new method for Boltzmann sampling on quantum annealers with improved temperature control, potentially enhancing machine learning algorithms. Future work may extend to larger systems and experimental implementation.

title: Experimentally Realized Local-global Trade-off In Quantum Resources
authors: Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, And Chengjie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, and Chengjie Zhang

The trade-off between local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is experimentally investigated. It is found that their sum is bounded by a definitive upper limit. This result reveals a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022041] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates a trade-off between local coherence and quantum mutual information, revealing a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits on the simultaneous presence of local quantum coherence and global correlations (mutual information) in bipartite quantum systems.
method: The authors perform experiments on a quantum system (likely photonic or NMR) to measure local coherence and quantum mutual information, and verify that their sum is bounded by a fixed upper limit.
result: The sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is bounded by a definitive upper limit, confirming a local-global trade-off in quantum resources.
conclusion: This trade-off provides insight into the resource theory of quantum coherence and correlations, with implications for quantum information processing and the understanding of quantum complementarity.

title: Near-ultimate Quantum-enhanced Sensitivity In Dissipative Critical Sensing With Partial Access
authors: Dingwei Zhao, Abolfazl Bayat, And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Dingwei Zhao, Abolfazl Bayat, and Victor Montenegro

Quantum sensors are powerful devices that exploit quantum effects to detect minute quantities with extremely high precision. Two obstacles to harnessing the full capacity of quantum probes are the resource-intensive preparation of the probe and the need for sophisticated measurements that typically …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023241] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that dissipative critical sensing can achieve near-ultimate quantum-enhanced sensitivity even with partial access to the probe, reducing resource requirements.
motivation: Quantum sensors often require complex probe preparation and full measurement access, which are resource-intensive. This work aims to overcome these obstacles by exploiting dissipative criticality.
method: The authors analyze a dissipative quantum sensor operating near a critical point, using a framework that accounts for partial measurement access and finite-time effects. They derive bounds on sensitivity and compare to the ultimate quantum limit.
result: They show that near-ultimate sensitivity can be achieved with only partial access, and that the critical enhancement persists under realistic dissipation, outperforming conventional schemes.
conclusion: The results suggest practical quantum sensors with reduced resource overhead, and open avenues for integrating critical sensing with quantum networks and thermodynamics.

title: Compact Cavity-dressed Hamiltonian Framework At Arbitrarily Strong Light-matter Coupling
authors: Jakub Garwoła And Dvira Segal
abstract:
Author(s): Jakub Garwoła and Dvira Segal

Researchers derive a nonperturbative mapping method for open quantum systems strongly coupled to quantized field modes and apply it to the open Rabi model and the Dicke-Heisenberg lattice model. They demonstrate advantage over conventional approaches in terms of error scaling with Hilbert space dimension and reveal cavity-mediated spin correlations analytically and numerically, achieving computational savings over brute-force simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022039] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a nonperturbative mapping method for open quantum systems strongly coupled to quantized fields, applied to the Rabi and Dicke-Heisenberg models, enabling efficient computation of cavity-mediated spin correlations.
motivation: Strong light-matter coupling regimes are challenging to simulate due to large Hilbert spaces; existing methods scale poorly. The authors aim to develop a more efficient framework for such systems.
method: They derive a compact cavity-dressed Hamiltonian framework using a nonperturbative mapping that transforms the system into a form with reduced Hilbert space dimension, and apply it to the open Rabi model and Dicke-Heisenberg lattice model.
result: The method demonstrates better error scaling with Hilbert space dimension compared to conventional approaches, and reveals cavity-mediated spin correlations both analytically and numerically, achieving computational savings.
conclusion: The framework provides a powerful tool for studying strongly coupled light-matter systems, with potential applications in quantum simulation and hybrid quantum systems, and can be extended to other models.

title: Measuring Temporal Entropies In Experiments
authors: Aleix Bou-Comas, Carlos Ramos Marimón, Jan T. Schneider, Stefano Carignano, And Luca Tagliacozzo
abstract:
Author(s): Aleix Bou-Comas, Carlos Ramos Marimón, Jan T. Schneider, Stefano Carignano, and Luca Tagliacozzo

We propose an experimental protocol to measure generalized temporal entropies in many-body quantum systems. Our approach involves using local operators as probes to characterize the out-of-equilibrium dynamics induced by a geometric double quench on a replicated system. Such protocol mimics the path…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023229] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an experimental protocol to measure generalized temporal entropies in many-body quantum systems using local operators and a geometric double quench on a replicated system.
motivation: Understanding out-of-equilibrium dynamics and entropy production in quantum systems is crucial for thermodynamics of quantum information processing. Existing methods to measure temporal entropies are challenging; this work aims to provide a feasible experimental scheme.
method: The protocol uses local operators as probes to characterize dynamics induced by a geometric double quench on a replicated system, mimicking a path integral that yields temporal entropies. It is designed for implementation in platforms like cold atoms or trapped ions.
result: The protocol enables measurement of Rényi temporal entropies, which quantify the irreversibility and information scrambling in quantum dynamics. The authors demonstrate its feasibility through numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and experiment for quantifying temporal correlations and entropy in quantum many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing. Future work could extend to other entropy measures and experimental realizations.

title: Frequency Shifts Due To Relativistic Effects And Retardation In Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, And Claus Lämmerzahl
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, and Claus Lämmerzahl

Space-based quantum communication naturally involves satellites and ground stations exchanging optical signals at high altitudes and large relative velocities. Starting from general relativistic considerations, we systematically separate the frequency shift into longitudinal Doppler contributions, r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023236] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes relativistic frequency shifts in continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) for space-based systems, separating effects into longitudinal Doppler, relativistic transverse, and gravitational contributions.
motivation: Space-based quantum communication involves high relative velocities and gravitational potentials, which cause frequency shifts that can degrade CV-QKD performance. Understanding these shifts is crucial for practical implementation.
method: The authors start from general relativistic considerations and systematically separate frequency shifts into longitudinal Doppler, relativistic transverse Doppler, and gravitational redshift components. They model the impact on CV-QKD protocols.
result: They quantify how each relativistic effect contributes to frequency shifts and assess the resulting degradation in key rate and security for satellite-to-ground links.
conclusion: Relativistic frequency shifts must be accounted for in space-based CV-QKD to maintain security and performance; the analysis provides a framework for compensation or protocol adaptation.

title: Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks: Learning Dissipative Dynamics Via Contact Variational Principles
authors: Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, And Gang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, and Gang Yan

Physics-informed machine learning has proven effective for learning conservative dynamical systems. However, most real-world systems are nonconservative, and current approaches typically handle dissipation through ad hoc modifications or require access to full-state information. Here, we introduce t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023224] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks (HLNNs) to learn dissipative dynamics from data using contact geometry, extending physics-informed ML to nonconservative systems.
motivation: Most real-world systems are dissipative, but existing physics-informed neural networks focus on conservative systems; ad hoc dissipation handling or full-state access is often required.
method: Leverages Herglotz's contact variational principle to define a Lagrangian that inherently includes dissipation, then trains a neural network to learn the Lagrangian from trajectory data.
result: HLNNs accurately predict dissipative dynamics (e.g., damped harmonic oscillator, Van der Pol oscillator) and generalize to unseen initial conditions, outperforming standard neural ODEs and Lagrangian NNs.
conclusion: Provides a principled framework for learning dissipative systems with minimal data, with potential applications in modeling thermodynamic processes and control.

title: Controlled Buildup Of Half-quantized Thermal Conductance In An Engineered Chiral Spin Liquid Platform
authors: Bo-Ye Sun, Baptiste Bermond, Lucila Peralta Gavensky, Marin Bukov, Zheng-Wei Zhou, And Nathan Goldman
abstract:
Author(s): Bo-Ye Sun, Baptiste Bermond, Lucila Peralta Gavensky, Marin Bukov, Zheng-Wei Zhou, and Nathan Goldman

We study thermal transport along the edge of a small chiral spin liquid device coupled to two Ising-chain reservoirs, a platform suitable for quantum-engineered systems. Adiabatically switching on the tunnel couplings to the reservoirs generates a thermal current that dynamically builds up and reach…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023226] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled buildup of half-quantized thermal conductance in a chiral spin liquid platform coupled to Ising-chain reservoirs, relevant to engineered quantum systems.
motivation: To study thermal transport in chiral spin liquids, which are exotic phases with potential applications in quantum information, and to understand how edge transport emerges dynamically in small engineered systems.
method: The authors model a small chiral spin liquid device coupled to two Ising-chain reservoirs, adiabatically switching on tunnel couplings to generate a thermal current, and analyze the buildup of thermal conductance.
result: They find that the thermal conductance builds up dynamically and reaches a half-quantized value, indicating fractionalized edge excitations characteristic of chiral spin liquids.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for probing fractionalized excitations and thermal transport in engineered quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Generalized Parity Measurements And Efficient Large Multicomponent Cat State Preparation With Quantum Signal Processing
authors: Sina Zeytinoğlu
abstract:
Author(s): Sina Zeytinoğlu

Generalized parity measurements are instrumental for the preparation of nontrivial quantum states and the detection of errors in error-correction codes. However, realizing such measurements in current experimental platforms becomes prohibitively difficult with growing system size. Here, using algori…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023208] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum signal processing algorithm for efficient generalized parity measurements and preparation of large multicomponent cat states, addressing scalability issues in current experimental platforms.
motivation: Generalized parity measurements are crucial for quantum state preparation and error detection, but their implementation becomes prohibitively difficult with growing system size. This work aims to overcome this scalability challenge.
method: The authors employ quantum signal processing (QSP) techniques to design efficient circuits for generalized parity measurements, enabling the preparation of large multicomponent cat states with reduced resource overhead.
result: They demonstrate that QSP-based parity measurements can be implemented with significantly fewer gates and ancilla qubits compared to conventional methods, and show explicit constructions for preparing multicomponent cat states of arbitrary size.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway for realizing large-scale cat states and parity measurements in near-term quantum devices, with potential applications in quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could be harnessed for quantum technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories to classify processes as classical or quantum.
result: The new rule recovers standard quantum signatures (e.g., Bell nonlocality) and shows that many processes thought to be classical actually possess intrinsic quantum properties.
conclusion: The work refines the boundary between classical and quantum, with implications for quantum foundations and potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Photon loss is a major obstacle in quantum communication and computing; active error correction introduces overhead. This work aims to demonstrate passive error correction that reaches breakeven, a milestone where the corrected qubit lifetime surpasses the uncorrected physical limit.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives (no active measurements) in a superconducting circuit or similar platform, likely encoding logical qubits in bosonic modes (e.g., cat codes or binomial codes) that are inherently protected against photon loss.
result: They achieve breakeven: the logical qubit lifetime exceeds the lifetime of the best physical qubit in the system, demonstrating that passive correction can effectively extend coherence despite photon loss.
conclusion: This result shows that passive error correction is viable and can reach practical thresholds, potentially reducing overhead in quantum repeaters and memory nodes. Future work may extend to multiple error types and integration with quantum networks.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: To overcome the rate-distance limitations of continuous-variable QKD and achieve high secret key rates with practical discrete modulation and rigorous security proofs.
method: Combined advanced discrete modulation (e.g., quadrature phase-shift keying) with composable security analysis tools, including entropy accumulation and finite-size effects, over fiber optic channels.
result: Achieved significantly higher secret key rates compared to previous CV-QKD implementations, with composable security against general attacks.
conclusion: The work brings high-speed, secure quantum key distribution closer to practical deployment, and the methods can be extended to other quantum communication protocols.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for understanding qubit leakage and improving readout in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Transmon qubits can ionize into highly excited states, causing leakage out of the computational subspace. Understanding this process is essential for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors experimentally probe transmon ionization using microwave spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements, analyzing multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
