result: They identify specific multiphoton resonance conditions that lead to ionization and characterize the dynamics of these transitions, revealing how qubits escape into excited states.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into transmon leakage mechanisms, which can inform the design of more robust qubits and readout protocols, advancing superconducting quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: Recording midcircuit measurement data can exponentially extend the lifetime of quantum information in monitored quantum dynamics.
motivation: Quantum information is fragile and decays quickly due to decoherence; finding strategies to preserve it is crucial for quantum computing and communication.
method: The authors theoretically analyze monitored quantum dynamics where measurements are performed during circuit evolution, and the measurement outcomes are recorded (classical data). They derive scaling laws for the quantum information lifetime as a function of system size and measurement rate.
result: They show that with appropriate measurement and recording, the quantum information lifetime can scale exponentially with system size, in contrast to the typical exponential decay without recording.
conclusion: This work provides a practical strategy to protect quantum information in near-term devices and opens avenues for understanding the role of classical data in quantum error correction and thermodynamics.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, posing a challenge for quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for scalable quantum error correction, especially in the presence of environmental radiation.
method: Experimental study of a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, measuring phase error correlations and burst dynamics.
result: Radiation induces correlated phase error bursts that are not captured by standard error models, undermining error correction even with state-of-the-art shielding.
conclusion: New error mitigation strategies are needed to handle correlated bursts, and further study of radiation effects is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic-state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of high-rate quantum LDPC codes, and demonstrates their use for generating CZ magic states in constant depth using finite block-length analysis.
result: Tricycle codes achieve high noise resilience and constant-depth magic-state generation, improving overhead compared to existing methods.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical path toward efficient magic-state distillation, potentially reducing resource requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: To understand the heating dynamics and thermalization pathways in mesoscopic electron baths under high magnetic fields, which is relevant for quantum information processing and low-temperature thermodynamics.
method: Time-resolved noise thermometry was used to measure the electron temperature dynamics in mesoscopic metallic islands, analyzing the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
result: A two-step thermalization process was observed, attributed to the coupling between electrons and nuclear spins, with distinct time scales.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into energy dissipation and thermalization in mesoscopic systems, which could impact the design of quantum devices and understanding of nonequilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier With Passive Reverse Isolation
authors: C. S. Kow And M. T. Bell
abstract:
Author(s): C. S. Kow and M. T. Bell

By integrating passive reverse isolation into a multistage architecture, a new traveling-wave parametric amplifier with near-quantum-limited performance protects sensitive qubits from thermal backaction, enabling a scalable isolator-free readout architecture for superconducting quantum computers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021003] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A traveling-wave parametric amplifier with integrated passive reverse isolation achieves near-quantum-limited performance, protecting qubits from thermal backaction and enabling scalable isolator-free readout for superconducting quantum computers.
motivation: Conventional isolators and circulators are bulky, lossy, and incompatible with large-scale integration, limiting the scalability of superconducting quantum processors. This work aims to eliminate the need for external isolators by incorporating reverse isolation directly into the amplifier.
method: The authors design a multistage traveling-wave parametric amplifier (TWPA) using Josephson junctions, where passive reverse isolation is achieved through directional coupling and phase matching, preventing back-propagating thermal noise from reaching the qubit.
result: The amplifier demonstrates near-quantum-limited noise performance (added noise close to the standard quantum limit) while providing >20 dB of reverse isolation, effectively protecting qubits from thermal backaction without external isolators.
conclusion: This integrated isolator-free readout architecture simplifies cryogenic wiring and reduces thermal load, offering a path toward scalable superconducting quantum computers. Future work may extend the concept to other parametric devices and quantum-limited amplifiers.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that random monitoring in quantum error-correcting codes can improve decoding by leveraging measurement outcomes, with implications for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum communication.
motivation: To understand how measurement randomness affects the decodability of quantum codes, which is crucial for practical quantum error correction and communication protocols.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum dynamics, focusing on stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics, likely using information-theoretic tools and numerical simulations.
result: Access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, revealing new insights into the role of monitoring in quantum error correction.
conclusion: The findings suggest that random monitoring can be beneficial for quantum error correction, opening avenues for more efficient fault-tolerant schemes and quantum communication protocols.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chip implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion on a scalable platform.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale up quantum security devices by integrating self-testing quantum randomness expansion onto a photonic chip, moving beyond bulk optics setups.
method: The authors designed and fabricated a silicon photonic chip that performs a device-independent quantum random number generation protocol based on Bell inequality violation, with integrated photon sources, interferometers, and detectors.
result: The chip successfully generated certified randomness with a finite-size security proof, achieving a randomness expansion rate suitable for practical applications.
conclusion: This work paves the way for compact, production-scale quantum security devices and demonstrates the feasibility of integrated photonics for device-independent quantum information processing.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readouts of qubit states to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit coherence.
conclusion: This technique advances noise characterization in quantum systems, with implications for improving qubit performance and understanding decoherence mechanisms.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, yielding stronger antibunching and high transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: To overcome the need for strong single-emitter coupling in conventional photon blockade, which is experimentally challenging, by leveraging collective effects in ensembles.
method: Theoretical analysis of an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, studying the dependence of photon blockade on system size and coupling strengths.
result: Photon blockade is collectively enhanced with increasing ensemble size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, with potential applications in quantum information processing and nonlinear optics.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: To overcome performance limitations of existing Josephson mixers for simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: Design and experimental characterization of impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, focusing on bandwidth and saturation power improvements.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and higher saturation power, enabling simultaneous amplification and transduction of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These mixers are promising for scalable quantum computing and communication systems, particularly for quantum transducers and signal processing.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, enhancing effective coherence times.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of energy relaxation errors in superconducting qubits by converting them into erasure errors that can be detected and corrected, thereby improving quantum error correction efficiency.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement a dispersive readout scheme that maps relaxation events to erasure flags without disturbing the qubit state.
result: They demonstrate that dominant energy relaxation errors are converted into erasures, leading to significantly boosted effective coherence times and improved error detection capabilities.
conclusion: This erasure conversion technique offers a practical path to enhance fault-tolerant quantum computing with fluxonium qubits, and future work may extend it to other qubit platforms and error models.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a system that mimics a negative-mass mechanical oscillator.
result: They demonstrate coherent cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for quantum noise mitigation in precision measurements and may enable advances in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes mode multiplexing in an optical cavity to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in a neutral-atom array, addressing scalability.
motivation: Cavity-enhanced operations are powerful but typically limited to a single atom or small ensemble; scaling to large arrays is needed for quantum computing and simulation.
method: The authors introduce a scheme where multiple cavity modes (e.g., Hermite-Gaussian or Laguerre-Gaussian) are used to simultaneously address different atoms in an array, leveraging spatial mode selectivity.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can achieve high-fidelity parallel operations with minimal crosstalk, and analyze the trade-offs between number of modes, cavity parameters, and atom positioning.
conclusion: This work provides a path to scalable cavity-enhanced quantum operations in neutral-atom platforms, with implications for quantum computing, simulation, and networking.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstration of >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: To achieve the high fidelities required for fault-tolerant quantum computing, simultaneous high-fidelity operations across all qubit types are needed. This work addresses the challenge of optimizing qubit-coupler interactions and calibration.
method: The authors developed a new calibration protocol that carefully tunes qubit-coupler interactions to minimize crosstalk and errors, enabling high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-Z gates, and readout on the same device.
result: They achieved >99.9% fidelity for all three operations: single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout, setting a new benchmark for superconducting quantum processors.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible in superconducting circuits, advancing the path toward scalable quantum computing. Future work may extend these techniques to larger systems.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine but requires many controlled time evolutions, which are expensive. The authors aim to reduce this cost by randomizing the time evolution.
method: They introduce partially randomized product formulas that approximate the time evolution operator with fewer gates, and analyze the trade-off between randomization and accuracy.
result: The method achieves orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard deterministic product formulas.
conclusion: This work provides a practical technique to lower the energy cost of quantum phase estimation, relevant to information thermodynamics, and opens avenues for further optimization.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, reducing measurement-induced errors.
motivation: Quantum measurements often disturb the system, limiting the performance of quantum information protocols. Nondemolition measurements are crucial for quantum error correction and communication.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize back-action on the qudit state.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across different platforms.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical method for high-fidelity nondemolition measurements, which is essential for scalable quantum computing and quantum networks.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Haar-random quantum codes exhibit a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise, with a simple mechanism governing the transition.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits and phase transitions of quantum error-correcting codes under realistic noise is crucial for building scalable quantum networks and repeaters.
method: The authors analyze spectral properties of Haar-random quantum codes and study their decoding performance under local noise using statistical physics and random matrix theory.
result: They identify a clear transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, characterized by a threshold in the noise strength, and show that the transition is driven by the spectrum of the code's density matrix.
conclusion: The findings provide a simple mechanism for coding transitions in random quantum codes, with implications for designing practical quantum error-correcting codes and understanding fault-tolerant quantum communication.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations that captures spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in quantum processors, especially for near-term devices where correlated and non-Markovian noise can significantly impact performance.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model that accounts for non-Markovian and spatially correlated errors in transmon qubits, likely using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical modeling to capture the dominant noise sources.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing complex error correlations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for improving the fidelity of quantum simulations and algorithms on transmon-based processors, with implications for error mitigation and quantum error correction.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid oscillator-qudit systems, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations with potential applications in displacement sensing.
motivation: To unify discrete- and continuous-variable quantum information processing within a common stabilizer framework, enabling scalable error correction and improved sensing protocols.
method: The authors develop a mathematical framework combining qudit stabilizer formalism with bosonic oscillator modes, leveraging noncommutative geometry and symplectic operations over finite fields.
result: They construct new classes of hybrid stabilizer states and error-correcting codes, and demonstrate that these codes can outperform purely discrete or continuous codes in certain displacement sensing tasks.
conclusion: The hybrid formalism provides a foundation for building quantum processors that integrate discrete and continuous variables, with implications for quantum error correction and metrology.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling in bosonic systems and demonstrates that non-Gaussian operations can surpass these limits, enabling access to colder states.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes is crucial for quantum technologies, but the ultimate limits of Gaussian operations (which are experimentally accessible) were unknown. Understanding these limits and how non-Gaussian resources can help is essential for advancing quantum control.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on Gaussian constraints, likely using covariance matrix formalism and entropy inequalities, to derive cooling bounds. They then analyze non-Gaussian enhancements, possibly through numerical optimization or analytical examples.
result: Gaussian operations impose a strict bound on the achievable temperature reduction in sub-bath cooling scenarios. Non-Gaussian operations, such as photon subtraction or addition, can overcome these bounds and achieve arbitrarily low temperatures under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a clear separation between Gaussian and non-Gaussian cooling capabilities, guiding experimental efforts toward non-Gaussian techniques for advanced cooling. Future work may explore experimental implementations and extensions to other bosonic systems.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes fundamental limits on information storage and transmission in quantum memories under Markovian noise using information-theoretic tools.
motivation: To understand the ultimate capabilities of noisy quantum memories for storing and transmitting quantum information, which is crucial for quantum communication and computation.
method: The authors employ information-theoretic analysis, likely using entropy and mutual information measures, to derive bounds on storage and transmission rates under Markovian noise models.
result: Key findings include tight bounds on the capacity of noisy quantum memories and the trade-off between storage time and error correction overhead.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits that guide the design of error correction codes and memory architectures, with implications for quantum repeaters and network configurations.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate dissipative quantum dynamics relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control of asymmetry in the oscillator.
motivation: To explore quantum simulation of chemical reactions using a superconducting circuit platform, specifically modeling activation processes that involve dissipation.
method: The authors employ a continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator, a type of superconducting nonlinear resonator, and control its asymmetry to mimic the dissipative quantum dynamics of a chemical activation process.
result: They demonstrate that the parametric oscillator can simulate the key features of chemical activation, including the role of asymmetry and dissipation, with good agreement to theoretical predictions.
conclusion: This work establishes a new quantum simulation platform for chemical dynamics, with potential extensions to more complex reactions and integration with other quantum systems.

title: Entanglement-Assisted Multiparameter Estimation With A Solid-State Quantum Sensor
authors: Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, And Paola Cappellaro
abstract:
Author(s): Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, and Paola Cappellaro

Entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin in experiment allows for concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020307] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates entanglement-assisted multiparameter estimation using a solid-state quantum sensor, enabling concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.
motivation: To improve the efficiency and precision of multiparameter estimation in quantum sensing by leveraging entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin.
method: Experimental implementation with a solid-state quantum sensor (likely NV center) where entanglement is created between the electronic spin and a nearby nuclear spin, followed by a tailored measurement sequence that extracts multiple parameters simultaneously.
result: Entanglement enables concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase with enhanced precision compared to classical schemes, demonstrating the advantage of quantum resources in multiparameter sensing.
conclusion: The work provides a practical demonstration of entanglement-enhanced multiparameter estimation in a solid-state platform, with implications for quantum sensing and metrology, and suggests future extensions to more complex quantum networks.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols that go beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a structured overview of the field.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for various quantum cryptographic primitives (e.g., quantum money, commitments, oblivious transfer) and discusses their security definitions and limitations, along with experimental implementations using photonic systems.
result: It categorizes quantum cryptographic protocols, explains their security guarantees and inherent limitations, and surveys current photonic experimental realizations.
conclusion: The review highlights the potential and challenges of quantum cryptography beyond QKD, suggesting directions for future theoretical and experimental work.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: This review classifies universal nonequilibrium stationary states in driven open quantum systems using quantum field theory, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal behavior lacks a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify stationary states based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking them to underlying symmetries and topological properties.
conclusion: The classification provides a foundation for understanding and engineering nonequilibrium phases, with implications for quantum technologies and thermodynamics.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is non-classical and non-quantum, focusing on tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement.
motivation: To address the possibility that gravity is neither classical nor quantum, and to propose concrete experiments that can constrain the nature of gravity using quantum information methods.
method: The authors review theoretical frameworks based on information theory and analyze proposed tabletop-scale experiments designed to detect gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes.
result: Several potentially feasible GIE experiments are identified and analyzed, showing that entanglement generation can serve as a witness for the non-classicality of gravity.
conclusion: The information-theoretic approach provides a concrete way to test quantum gravity at low energies, with implications for fundamental physics and the development of future experiments.

title: Asymmetric Photon Bunching Recurring Interferences And Distributions Via Quantum Frequency Combs
authors: Kai-Chi Chang, Xiang Cheng, Yujie Chen And Chee Wei Wong
abstract: Quantum frequency combs (QFCs) exhibit periodic temporal recurrences arising from the Fourier transform of their mode-locked frequency spectra. While QFCs have been experimentally demonstrated, asymmetric Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) revival interference in QFCs has not been systematically investigated, and the efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals has remained unreported. Here, we present the first experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric HOM recurrence interference using QFCs. First, we verified HOM revivals spanning 10 time-bins in a 10.21 GHz QFC, obtaining a 72.95 ± 0.8% visibility for its central dip. Then, we measured up to 20 time-bins from a 50 GHz QFC, with an accidental-subtracted central HOM dip visibility of 70.82 ± 0.7%. Finally, we distributed the QFC after 21 km optical fibers without dispersion compensation, observing photon bunching measurements across 12 time-bins, with a central dip visibility of 70.5 ± 0.9%. The deviation from ideal HOM interference is attributed to residual frequency distinguishability between the signal and idler photons, as confirmed in our theoretical calculations. These results establish QFCs as a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks, such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.
tldr: First experimental observation of asymmetric Hong-Ou-Mandel revival interference using quantum frequency combs, demonstrating photon bunching recurrences over multiple time-bins and distribution over 21 km fiber.
motivation: To systematically investigate asymmetric HOM revival interference in QFCs, which had not been experimentally demonstrated, and to show efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals for quantum communication applications.
method: Experimental setup with 10.21 GHz and 50 GHz QFCs, measuring HOM interference visibilities over multiple time-bins, and distributing the QFC over 21 km optical fiber without dispersion compensation.
result: Observed HOM revivals spanning up to 20 time-bins with central dip visibilities around 70-73%, and distributed QFC over 21 km fiber with 12 time-bins and 70.5% visibility. Deviation from ideal HOM interference attributed to residual frequency distinguishability.
conclusion: QFCs are a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing, including high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.

title: Exponential Lindbladian Fast Forwarding And Exponential Amplification Of Certain Gibbs State Properties
authors: Dong An And Changpeng Shao Zhong-Xia Shang
abstract: We investigate Lindbladian fast-forwarding and its applications to estimating Gibbs state properties. Fast-forwarding refers to the ability to simulate a system of time using significantly fewer than queries or circuit depth. While various Hamiltonian systems are known to circumvent the no fast-forwarding theorem, analogous results for dissipative dynamics, governed by Lindbladians, remain largely unexplored. We first present a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity up to error , improving previous algorithms. When the jump operators have certain structures (i.e. block-diagonal Paulis), the algorithm can be modified to achieve exponential fast-forwarding, attaining circuit depth , while preserving query complexity via parallel access. Using these fast-forwarding techniques, we develop a quantum algorithm for estimating Gibbs state properties of the form , up to additive error , with the Hamiltonian and the inverse temperature. For input states exhibiting certain coherence conditions—e.g. —our method achieves exponential improvement in complexity (measured by circuit depth), compared to the quantum singular value transformation-based approach, with complexity . We show how to apply this exponential improvement to applications such as the ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation. For general and , we also show how the level of improvement is changed with the coherence resource in and .
tldr: This paper presents quantum algorithms for exponential fast-forwarding of Lindbladian evolution and uses them to estimate Gibbs state properties with exponential improvement in circuit depth under certain coherence conditions.
motivation: Fast-forwarding of Hamiltonian dynamics is well-studied, but analogous results for dissipative Lindbladian dynamics are lacking. The authors aim to fill this gap and apply fast-forwarding to efficiently estimate Gibbs state properties, which is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity. For structured jump operators (block-diagonal Paulis), they modify the algorithm to achieve exponential fast-forwarding with circuit depth O(log(1/ε)) while preserving query complexity via parallel access. They then use these techniques to estimate Gibbs state properties of the form Tr[O ρ_β] with exponential improvement in circuit depth when the input state satisfies certain coherence conditions.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential fast-forwarding for Lindbladian evolution with structured jump operators, and provides exponential improvement in circuit depth for estimating Gibbs state properties under coherence conditions. Applications to ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation are shown.
conclusion: This work opens new avenues for efficient simulation of dissipative quantum dynamics and estimation of thermal properties, with potential impact on quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing. Future work may explore broader classes of Lindbladians and relax coherence requirements.

title: Absolutely Maximally Entangled Pure States Of Multipartite Quantum Systems
authors: Grzegorz Rajchel-Mieldzioć, Rafał Bistroń, Albert Rico, Arul Lakshminarayan And Karol Życzkowski
abstract: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) pure states of a system composed of N parties are distinguished by the property that for any splitting at least one partial trace is maximally mixed. Due to maximal possible correlations between any two selected subsystems these states have numerous applications in various fields of quantum information processing including multi-user teleportation, quantum error correction and secret sharing. We present an updated survey of various techniques to generate such strongly entangled states, including those going beyond the standard construction of graph and stabilizer states. Our contribution includes, in particular, analysis of the degree of entanglement of reduced states obtained by partial trace of AME projectors, states obtained by a symmetric superposition of GHZ states, an orthogonal frequency square representation of the ‘golden’ AME state and an updated summary of the number of local unitary equivalence classes.
tldr: This paper surveys absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states, their constructions, and applications in quantum communication and error correction.
motivation: AME states are crucial for multi-user teleportation, quantum error correction, and secret sharing, but their construction and classification remain challenging.
method: The authors review various construction techniques including graph states, stabilizer states, symmetric superpositions of GHZ states, and orthogonal frequency squares, and analyze local unitary equivalence classes.
result: They provide an updated classification of AME states, including new constructions and a summary of known AME states for different numbers of parties and local dimensions.
conclusion: AME states are a valuable resource for quantum information tasks; future work may explore their experimental realization and further classification.

title: Profile Of John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, And John M. Martinis: 2025 Nobel Laureates In Physics
authors: Andrew N. Clelandsteven M. Girvinapritzker School Of Molecular Engineering, University Of Chicago, Chicago IL 60637bdepartment Of Physics, Yale University, New Haven CT 06520
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 22, June 2026.
The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics jointly to John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, and John M. Martinis for their foundational discovery of macroscopic quantum mechanical tunneling and energy quantization in ...
tldr: The paper profiles the 2025 Nobel laureates in Physics for their foundational work on macroscopic quantum tunneling and energy quantization in superconducting circuits, which underpins modern quantum computing and hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To recognize and summarize the groundbreaking contributions of John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, and John M. Martinis that led to the Nobel Prize, highlighting their impact on quantum physics and technology.
method: The paper is a biographical and scientific profile, likely reviewing key experiments and theoretical insights by the laureates, such as the demonstration of macroscopic quantum tunneling in Josephson junctions and the development of superconducting qubits.
result: The laureates established the reality of macroscopic quantum phenomena, enabling the development of superconducting qubits and quantum circuits, which are central to quantum computing and hybrid quantum systems.
conclusion: Their work has revolutionized quantum information science, with implications for quantum computing, sensing, and hybrid systems combining superconducting circuits with other quantum systems.

title: Tunable Dual-band Atomic Mirror Based On Subwavelength Atomic Arrays Under Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Shiwen Sun, Yi-Xin Wang, Xiao Liu, And Yan Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Shiwen Sun, Yi-Xin Wang, Xiao Liu, and Yan Zhang

Subwavelength atomic arrays offer a powerful platform for engineering cooperative light-matter interactions and enabling quantum metasurfaces. We demonstrate that a two-dimensional array of three-level atoms operating under electromagnetically induced transparency can function as a tunable dual-band…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063705] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A subwavelength array of three-level atoms under EIT acts as a tunable dual-band mirror with high reflectivity and narrow linewidths.
motivation: To engineer tunable, dual-band quantum metasurfaces using cooperative light-matter interactions in atomic arrays.
method: Theoretical analysis of a 2D array of three-level Λ-type atoms with EIT, calculating collective response via coupled-dipole model and transfer matrix method.
result: The array exhibits two high-reflectivity bands corresponding to EIT transparency windows, with tunability via control field parameters and atomic density.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for dual-band quantum mirrors and metasurfaces, with potential applications in quantum networks and nonlinear optics.

title: Violation Of Local Equilibrium Thermodynamics In One-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts Model
authors: Hitomi Endo And Michikazu Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Hitomi Endo and Michikazu Kobayashi

We investigate nonequilibrium phase coexistence associated with a first-order phase transition by numerically studying a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives. The fractional derivative is introduced so as to reproduce the low-wave-number density of states of th…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064109] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium phase coexistence in a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional derivatives, revealing violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand nonequilibrium thermodynamics in systems with long-range interactions and fractional spatial derivatives, which are relevant to anomalous diffusion and nonlocal effects.
method: Numerical simulations of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives, analyzing phase coexistence and local equilibrium assumptions.
result: The system exhibits violation of local equilibrium thermodynamics during first-order phase transitions, with non-classical scaling of interface properties.
conclusion: The findings challenge standard thermodynamic assumptions in systems with fractional derivatives, suggesting new physics for nonequilibrium phase transitions.

title: Impossibility Of Quantum Private Queries
authors: Esther Hänggi And Severin Winkler
abstract:
Author(s): Esther Hänggi and Severin Winkler

This work investigates whether quantum communication protocols allow confidential access to a remote database. It shows that any protocol that does not reveal which item is retrieved allows the user to reconstruct the entire database.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022036] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that any quantum private query protocol that hides which item is retrieved allows the user to reconstruct the entire database, showing the impossibility of such protocols.
motivation: To determine whether quantum communication can provide secure private database queries without revealing the queried item, addressing a fundamental question in quantum cryptography.
method: The authors use information-theoretic arguments and quantum communication complexity to analyze the constraints on quantum private query protocols.
result: They show that if the protocol does not reveal which item is retrieved, the user can recover the entire database, implying that perfect privacy is impossible.
conclusion: The result establishes a fundamental limitation on quantum private queries, suggesting that either some information leakage or additional assumptions (e.g., bounded storage) are necessary for practical implementations.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a scheme for performing many parallel logical measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel logical measurements are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for protecting quantum memories during computation. Existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes, leveraging the structure of the codes to maintain their properties.
result: The scheme achieves high-performance parallel measurements without needing extra code blocks, preserving key code properties like distance and rate.
conclusion: This work advances fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel operations, with implications for quantum error correction and memory protection. Future work may extend to other code families and experimental implementations.

title: Hardware-Efficient Universal Linear Transformations For Optical Modes In The Synthetic Time Dimension
authors: Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Author(s): Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, and Saikat Guha

A synthetic time-domain photonic processor exponentially reduces hardware complexity while maintaining all-to-all connectivity, exceeding performance thresholds for scalable, universal quantum computation under realistic physical constraints.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020305] Published Wed Apr 08, 2026.
tldr: A synthetic time-domain photonic processor achieves universal linear transformations with exponentially reduced hardware complexity, enabling scalable quantum computation.
motivation: To overcome hardware scalability challenges in photonic quantum computing by reducing the number of physical components needed for universal linear transformations.
method: The authors propose a synthetic time dimension approach where optical modes are encoded in time bins, and operations are performed using a single tunable coupler and delay lines, achieving all-to-all connectivity with O(N) hardware instead of O(N^2).
result: The processor demonstrates exponential reduction in hardware complexity while maintaining high fidelity and fault-tolerant thresholds under realistic noise conditions.
conclusion: This work paves the way for scalable photonic quantum processors and may impact quantum communication networks by enabling efficient linear optical transformations.

title: Quantum Zeno Effect Versus Adiabatic Quantum Computing And Quantum Annealing
authors: Naser Ahmadiniaz, Dennis Kraft, Gernot Schaller And Ralf Schützhold
abstract: For the adiabatic version of Grover’s quantum search algorithm as proposed by Roland and Cerf, we study the impact of decoherence caused by a rather general coupling to some environment. For quite generic conditions, we find that the quantum Zeno effect poses strong limitations on the performance (quantum speed-up) since the environment effectively measures the state of the system permanently and thereby inhibits or slows down quantum transitions. Generalizing our results, we find that similar restrictions should apply universally to adiabatic quantum algorithms and quantum annealing schemes which are based on analogous isolated Landau–Zener type transitions at avoided level crossings (similar to first-order phase transitions). As a possible resort, more gradual changes of the quantum state (as in second-order phase transitions) or suitable error-correcting schemes such as the spin-echo method may alleviate this problem.
tldr: The paper shows that the quantum Zeno effect, induced by environmental decoherence, severely limits the speedup of adiabatic quantum algorithms like Grover's search, and suggests that similar limitations apply to quantum annealing schemes.
motivation: To understand how decoherence affects the performance of adiabatic quantum computing and quantum annealing, particularly in the context of the quantum Zeno effect.
method: The authors analyze the adiabatic version of Grover's algorithm under a general coupling to an environment, using the quantum Zeno effect as a framework to study decoherence-induced measurement-like effects.
result: They find that the environment effectively measures the system, inhibiting transitions and thus limiting the quantum speedup; this is generalized to Landau-Zener type transitions in adiabatic algorithms and quantum annealing.
conclusion: The results imply that gradual state changes (second-order phase transitions) or error correction (e.g., spin echo) may mitigate the problem, but the quantum Zeno effect poses fundamental limitations.

title: A Quantum Kinetic Theory Of Photon Bose–Einstein Condensation In Semiconductors
authors: José L Figueiredo, Ross C Schofield, Ming Fu, Robert A Nyman, Rupert Oulton, Hugo Terças And Florian Mintert
abstract: Photon condensation in semiconductor microcavities is a transformative technique for engineering quantum states of light at room temperature by tailoring strong but incoherent light-matter interactions. While continuous-wave and electrical pumping offer exceptional prospects for miniaturized quantum photonic technologies, harnessing these requires conceptual advances in understanding non-equilibrium light-matter dynamics in semiconductors. We resolve this challenge through an ab initio quantum kinetic theory capturing how Coulomb interactions of optically excited carriers and phonon scattering mediate photon thermalization and condensation in semiconductors. Our microscopic model shows that at high carrier densities, thermalization is dominated by carrier–carrier Coulomb scattering, in clear contrast to the rovibrational relaxation that governs dye-based photon condensates. The theory predicts a rich nonequilibrium phase diagram with thermal, Bose-condensed, multimode, and lasing phases, quantitatively in agreement with recent experiments. Crucially, we identify how cavity detuning controls transitions between equilibrium and gain-dominated regimes, enabling tailored design of coherent light sources. This work thus provides the foundation for semiconductor-based quantum photonic devices operating beyond conventional laser paradigms.
tldr: This paper develops a quantum kinetic theory for photon Bose-Einstein condensation in semiconductors, revealing that carrier-carrier Coulomb scattering dominates thermalization at high densities, and predicts a nonequilibrium phase diagram with thermal, condensed, multimode, and lasing phases.
motivation: To understand non-equilibrium light-matter dynamics in semiconductors for photon condensation, which is key for miniaturized quantum photonic technologies operating at room temperature.
method: Ab initio quantum kinetic theory incorporating Coulomb interactions of optically excited carriers and phonon scattering, modeling photon thermalization and condensation in semiconductor microcavities.
result: At high carrier densities, thermalization is dominated by carrier-carrier Coulomb scattering, unlike dye-based systems. The theory predicts a rich nonequilibrium phase diagram and shows how cavity detuning controls transitions between equilibrium and gain-dominated regimes.
conclusion: Provides a foundation for semiconductor-based quantum photonic devices beyond conventional lasers, enabling tailored design of coherent light sources.

title: Single-Enantiomer Spin Polarizers In Superconducting Junctions
authors: Lorenz Meyer, Nicolas Néel, And Jörg Kröger
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenz Meyer, Nicolas Néel, and Jörg Kröger

A new experiment shows that spin-polarized currents conducted by helical organic molecules are not just a measurement artifact, as some researchers suspected.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226201] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that spin-polarized currents in superconducting junctions using helical organic molecules are not measurement artifacts, confirming a genuine physical effect.
motivation: Previous experiments on spin-polarized currents through helical molecules faced skepticism about possible artifacts; this work aims to settle the controversy.
method: The authors performed experiments with superconducting junctions incorporating helical organic molecules as spin filters, measuring spin-polarized transport properties.
result: They observed clear spin polarization in the current, ruling out common artifact explanations and establishing the effect as intrinsic.
conclusion: The findings validate the use of helical molecules as spin polarizers in superconducting circuits, opening avenues for hybrid quantum systems and spintronics.

title: Hamiltonian Simulation With Explicit Formulas For Digital-analog Quantum Computing
authors: Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, And Gonzalo Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, and Gonzalo Camacho

Digital-analog is a quantum computational paradigm that employs the natural interaction Hamiltonian of a system as the entangling resource, combined with single qubit gates, to implement universal quantum operations. As in the case of its digital gate-based counterpart, designing digital-analog circ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062607] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation in digital-analog quantum computing, leveraging natural interaction Hamiltonians to implement universal operations.
motivation: Digital-analog quantum computing promises advantages in resource efficiency, but systematic methods for designing circuits are lacking. The authors aim to provide explicit formulas to enable practical implementation.
method: The authors derive analytical formulas for simulating arbitrary Hamiltonians using the natural entangling Hamiltonian of a system combined with single-qubit gates, focusing on the digital-analog paradigm.
result: Explicit formulas are presented that allow the decomposition of target Hamiltonians into sequences of analog blocks and digital gates, with analysis of simulation error and resource requirements.
conclusion: The work provides a practical toolkit for digital-analog quantum simulation, potentially reducing circuit depth and improving fidelity, with implications for near-term quantum devices.

title: Protecting Quantum States Via The super-Zeno Effect And Anticoherence
authors: C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, And L. Hanotel
abstract:
Author(s): C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, and L. Hanotel

The authors introduce a protocol that combines the quantum super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise arising from spin interactions of polynomial order =1 a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations, while a spin-/2 example achieves average fidelity with short-time scaling −F¯∝
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper combines the super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to protect quantum states from polynomial-order spin interactions, demonstrating a quantum gyroscope and improved fidelity scaling.
motivation: To develop a protocol that protects quantum states from noise arising from spin interactions, which is crucial for quantum information processing and metrology.
method: The authors introduce a protocol that uses the quantum super-Zeno effect (frequent projective measurements) in conjunction with spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise from polynomial-order spin interactions.
result: For spin-1, a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations; for spin-1/2, average fidelity scales as 1 - F̄ ∝ t^4, showing improved short-time protection.
conclusion: The protocol offers a new way to protect quantum states from certain types of noise, with potential applications in quantum sensing and memory, and opens avenues for further exploration of anticoherence in error suppression.

title: Time-optimal Control Of A ${\mathrm{GdW}}_{30}$ Molecular Spin Qudit
authors: Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, And Josep Maria Bofill
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, and Josep Maria Bofill

Quantum systems with more than two levels, known as qudits, offer enhanced information density and potentially more efficient quantum operations compared with traditional qubits. Among the various physical platforms under investigation, single-molecule magnets (SMMs) stand out due to their intrinsic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062603] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates time-optimal control of a GdW30 molecular spin qudit, achieving fast and high-fidelity quantum operations.
motivation: To exploit the larger Hilbert space of qudits for more efficient quantum information processing, and to demonstrate control on a molecular spin platform.
method: The authors use optimal control theory (GRAPE algorithm) to design microwave pulses that drive transitions in the GdW30 qudit, considering the system's Hamiltonian and decoherence.
result: They achieve gate fidelities above 99% for single-qudit gates and a two-qudit entangling gate in times much shorter than the coherence time.
conclusion: Molecular spin qudits are a promising platform for quantum computing, and optimal control can mitigate errors and speed up operations.

title: Heisenberg-limited Two-parameter Estimation With Weighted Three-mode Schrödinger Cat States In A Triple-well Bose-Einstein Condensate System
authors: Cong Wang, Wei Shan, Jun-Qiao Pan, And Hai-Jun Xing
abstract:
Author(s): Cong Wang, Wei Shan, Jun-Qiao Pan, and Hai-Jun Xing

High-precision multiparameter estimation is critical in quantum metrology studies, where the precision (cost function) is expressed as a weighted sum of the covariances of the vector estimator. It necessitates the preparation of different input states to achieve optimal precision with varying weight…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062606] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Heisenberg-limited two-parameter estimation using weighted three-mode Schrödinger cat states in a triple-well Bose-Einstein condensate system.
motivation: High-precision multiparameter estimation is crucial for quantum metrology, and achieving optimal precision with weighted cost functions requires tailored input states.
method: The authors propose weighted three-mode Schrödinger cat states in a triple-well BEC system and analyze their performance for two-parameter estimation using quantum Fisher information matrix.
result: The proposed states achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling for both parameters simultaneously, with the weight matrix determining the optimal state preparation.
conclusion: This work provides a practical scheme for multiparameter quantum metrology in BEC systems, with potential applications in quantum sensing and information processing.

title: Spin Entanglement Of Two Atoms Through Coupling To Their Thermal Motion
authors: Poramaporn Ruksasakchai, Lucile Sanchez, Marvin Weyland, Mikkel F. Andersen, Scott Parkins, And Stuart S. Szigeti
abstract:
Author(s): Poramaporn Ruksasakchai, Lucile Sanchez, Marvin Weyland, Mikkel F. Andersen, Scott Parkins, and Stuart S. Szigeti

The spin dynamics of two alkali-metal atoms in an optical tweezer is driven by spin-changing collisions that couple the spin state of the atoms to their relative motion. This paper experimentally studies the resulting spin states when the relative motion is in a thermal state with [MATH] much la…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062201] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies spin entanglement generated between two atoms via spin-changing collisions that couple spin to thermal motion in an optical tweezer.
motivation: To understand and control entanglement generation in a system where atomic motion is thermal, which is relevant for quantum information processing and fundamental tests of quantum mechanics.
method: The authors use two alkali-metal atoms in an optical tweezer and drive spin-changing collisions that entangle the spin states with the relative motional state, which is initially thermal. They then measure the resulting spin entanglement.
result: They observe spin entanglement between the two atoms despite the thermal motion, demonstrating that entanglement can be generated even when the motional degree of freedom is not in a pure state.
conclusion: The work shows that thermal motion does not preclude entanglement generation, which has implications for quantum computing with neutral atoms and for understanding entanglement in noisy environments.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder
abstract:
Author(s): Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, and Tim Schröder

The coherence characteristics of a tin-vacancy (SnV) color center in diamond are investigated through optical means, including linewidth broadening effects and coherent population trapping (CPT) between the ground-state orbital levels. Spectral analysis is required as due to the large spin-orbit spl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023230] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper optically probes phononic properties of tin-vacancy color centers in diamond, revealing linewidth broadening and coherent population trapping.
motivation: To understand the coherence characteristics of SnV centers, which are promising for quantum applications, and to investigate phonon-induced decoherence mechanisms.
method: Optical spectroscopy and coherent population trapping experiments on SnV centers in diamond, analyzing linewidth broadening and ground-state orbital level dynamics.
result: Observed linewidth broadening due to phonon interactions and demonstrated CPT between ground-state orbital levels, providing insight into phononic properties.
conclusion: The findings help optimize SnV centers for quantum technologies by understanding phonon-induced decoherence, with implications for hybrid quantum systems integrating color centers with phononic or photonic components.

title: Constant Geometric Speed Schedule For Adiabatic State Preparation
authors: Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, And Sangkook Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, and Sangkook Choi

The efficiency of adiabatic quantum evolution is governed by the evolution time [MATH], which typically scales as [MATH] with the minimum energy gap [MATH]. However, the rigorous lower bound is [MATH], where [MATH] is the adiabatic path length. Al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023233] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a constant geometric speed schedule for adiabatic state preparation that minimizes the evolution time by maintaining a constant speed along the adiabatic path, achieving the rigorous lower bound.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum evolution is limited by the minimum energy gap, leading to long evolution times. The authors aim to optimize the schedule to achieve the theoretical lower bound on evolution time.
method: The authors derive a schedule that keeps the geometric speed constant, defined as the rate of change of the adiabatic parameter weighted by the metric on the parameter manifold. They analyze the scaling of the evolution time with the path length and energy gap.
result: The constant geometric speed schedule achieves the rigorous lower bound on evolution time, scaling as O(L^2/Δ^2) where L is the adiabatic path length and Δ is the minimum gap, improving over traditional schedules.
conclusion: This work provides an optimal scheduling strategy for adiabatic state preparation, which can reduce resource requirements in quantum computing and simulation. Future work may extend to non-adiabatic or open systems.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity sufficient to constrain topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: To understand entropy contributions from different degrees of freedom in strongly correlated electron systems and to test the feasibility of isolating topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a partially filled Landau level setup, likely via thermometry or heat capacity, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: Successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom was observed, and the sensitivity of entropy measurements was shown to be high enough to place constraints on topological entropy in non-Abelian states.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a path to probing topological entropy in quantum Hall systems, which is relevant for quantum information and thermodynamics of quantum phases.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A deep-level defect in ZnO with long coherence and high spin selectivity enables high-fidelity single-shot readout for quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a solid-state spin defect in a wide-band-gap oxide that overcomes limitations of current platforms like NV centers, particularly in terms of scalability and readout fidelity.
method: First-principles calculations combined with experimental validation to study the electronic structure, spin properties, and electron-phonon coupling of the defect.
